question.worked_solution:
First, we write the equation in standard form by bringing all of the terms to the left-hand side. This gives the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+22(x+1) & =-100 \\ {x}^{2}+22x+22+100 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+22x+122 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the roots of a quadratic equation using the quadratic formula:

$$
x=\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a}
$$

In this case, the coefficients are $a=1,\,b=22,$ and $c=122.$ Substituting these values into the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{-22\pm \sqrt{(22)^{2}-4(1)(122)}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{-22\pm \sqrt{484-488}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-22\pm \sqrt{-4}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-22\pm 2\,\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-11\pm 1\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=-11+\text{i}$ and $x=-11-\text{i}.$
